meta.scope: Mexico batch 6 — larger set (14 candidates): victimization & urban security surveys, state economic activity & state exports, business directory, social security (IMSS/ISSSTE), key social pensions / Bienestar transfers. Continues expansion toward 150+ under the new broader node definition.
meta.confidence_note: All items below are well-documented recurring publications or clearly load-bearing static frameworks with ongoing citation. Thin or purely administrative registers without published statistical series were not included.

candidates.title: Encuesta Nacional de Victimización y Percepción sobre Seguridad Pública (ENVIPE)
candidates.description: Annual household survey estimating crime prevalence, incidence, dark figure (cifra negra), characteristics of victims and crimes, economic and social impact of crime, perception of public security, and trust/performance of security and justice institutions. National and state representativeness. Part of the SNIGSPIJ.
candidates.notes: Flagship victimization survey (15th edition in 2025 covering 2024). 2025 results: 29.0% of households had at least one member who was a crime victim; 23.1 million people aged 18+ victimized. Measures trust in Marina, Army, Guardia Nacional, state and municipal police, etc. Explicitly framed as Información de Interés Nacional within the government/security/justice subsystem of the SNIEG.

candidates.title: Encuesta Nacional de Seguridad Pública Urbana (ENSU) / National Survey of Urban Public Security
candidates.description: Quarterly survey of perception of insecurity and related behaviours in selected urban areas (expanded set of cities). Complements ENVIPE with higher-frequency urban perception indicators, expectations about crime, and evaluation of security authorities.
candidates.notes: High-frequency companion to ENVIPE. June 2026 results showed perception of insecurity at 59.8% among adults in the covered urban areas. Tracks evaluation of Marina, Army, municipal police, etc., and household victimization of selected crimes in the reference semester.

candidates.title: Indicador Trimestral de la Actividad Económica Estatal (ITAEE) / Quarterly Indicator of State Economic Activity
candidates.description: Quarterly volume index of economic activity for each of the 32 federal entities. Part of the Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales de México. Provides the main short-term picture of state-level GDP-like activity.
candidates.notes: Core state-level activity indicator (base 2018). Published with seasonally adjusted and original series; ranks entities by quarterly and annual growth. Direct bridge from national SCNM to the state jurisdiction level.

candidates.title: Exportaciones Trimestrales por Entidad Federativa (ETEF) / Quarterly Exports by Federal Entity
candidates.description: Quarterly value of merchandise exports by federal entity (and by SCIAN sector/subsector). Shows each state’s contribution to Mexico’s external trade.
candidates.notes: Important regional trade series. Q1 2026 total ≈ USD 158 billion; Chihuahua, Jalisco, Coahuila, Nuevo León and Baja California typically dominate. Complements the national Balanza Comercial and links state activity to external demand (and indirectly to T-MEC utilisation patterns).

candidates.title: Directorio Estadístico Nacional de Unidades Económicas (DENUE) / National Statistical Directory of Economic Units
candidates.description: Statistical directory of economic units (establishments) with location, activity (SCIAN), size and other identifying variables. Updated periodically; used as sampling frame and public business-location resource. Methodological documents accompany each major update.
candidates.notes: Foundational business-frame product. Supports design of establishment surveys (EMIM, EMEC, EMS, ENEC, etc.) and is itself a disseminated statistical product with methodological documentation (e.g. 2026 update).

candidates.title: Puestos de trabajo afiliados al IMSS / IMSS-affiliated employment posts
candidates.description: Monthly administrative statistics of formal private-sector employment posts registered with the Mexican Social Security Institute. Reports permanent and temporary posts, average contribution wage, and employer registrations. Principal high-frequency indicator of formal private employment.
candidates.notes: Key formal-employment series. Mid-2026 figures around 22.8 million posts (majority permanent). Widely used alongside ENOE (which covers total employment including informal) to monitor labour-market formalisation. Average contribution wage also published.

candidates.title: Anuario Estadístico del ISSSTE / ISSSTE Statistical Yearbook
candidates.publisher: Instituto de Seguridad y Servicios Sociales de los Trabajadores del Estado (ISSSTE)
candidates.description: Annual statistical yearbook of the social-security institute covering public-sector workers. Includes population with entitlement (derechohabientes), pensions by type and regime, medical services and other benefits, with state detail.
candidates.notes: Main published statistical product for ISSSTE coverage and pensions. Complements IMSS data for a fuller picture of formal social-security affiliation (private vs public-sector workers).

candidates.title: Pensión para el Bienestar de las Personas Adultas Mayores
candidates.publisher: Secretaría del Bienestar / Gobierno de México
candidates.description: Universal (or near-universal) non-contributory pension for older adults. One of the largest social-transfer programmes. Coverage and payment statistics are published in official programme reports and inform poverty and income analyses.
candidates.notes: Major medical/social transfer programme. 2025 reporting indicated ~13.2 million older-adult beneficiaries with multi-hundred-billion-peso annual outlays. Directly relevant to household income, poverty reduction, and the ‘medical transfers / social protection’ theme. Complements contributory pensions (IMSS/ISSSTE) and ENIGH income data.

candidates.title: Pensión Mujeres Bienestar
candidates.publisher: Secretaría del Bienestar / Gobierno de México
candidates.description: Targeted non-contributory pension / support programme for women (specific age and eligibility rules). Coverage statistics published in Bienestar programme reports.
candidates.notes: Significant gender-focused transfer. 2025 figures cited ~3.0 million women beneficiaries. Part of the broader Bienestar transfer architecture that feeds into household income and poverty analysis.

candidates.title: Pensión para el Bienestar de las Personas con Discapacidad
candidates.publisher: Secretaría del Bienestar / Gobierno de México
candidates.description: Non-contributory disability support programme with universal coverage in a large set of states. Beneficiary counts published in official programme reporting.
candidates.notes: Completes the core trio of large Bienestar cash-transfer programmes (older adults, women, disability). 2025 coverage figures in the 1.6 million range. Relevant to social-protection and poverty analysis alongside ENIGH and multidimensional poverty measurement.

candidates.title: Indicador Mensual de la Actividad Industrial por Entidad Federativa (IMAIEF)
candidates.description: Monthly industrial activity indicator disaggregated by federal entity. Companion to the national IMAI; allows state-level tracking of mining, manufacturing, construction and utilities.
candidates.notes: State-level monthly industrial series. Extends the national IMAI framework to the entity level and is published on the regular INEGI calendar.

candidates.title: ENOE — Tasa de informalidad laboral / Labour informality rate (from ENOE)
candidates.description: Key labour-market indicator derived from the Encuesta Nacional de Ocupación y Empleo measuring the share of employed persons in informal employment. Published with the regular ENOE releases.
candidates.notes: Critical complement to formal-employment series (IMSS). Recent figures hover near 55% informality. Used in national-accounts informal-sector estimation and in social-policy analysis. Treated as a distinct high-value indicator node even though it is produced from ENOE microdata.

candidates.title: Cuentas por Sectores Institucionales (SCNM) / Institutional Sector Accounts
candidates.description: Annual institutional-sector accounts within the Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales de México (non-financial corporations, financial corporations, general government, households, non-profit institutions serving households, rest of the world). Provide the full sequence of current and accumulation accounts by sector.
candidates.notes: Detailed layer of the SCNM. Explicitly listed in methodology documents as part of the accounts produced under SNA 2008. Essential for fiscal, household-income and financial-balance analysis that goes beyond GDP aggregates.

candidates.title: Matriz de Insumo-Producto (MIP) / Input-Output Matrix
candidates.description: Symmetric input-output table produced as part of the national accounts benchmark process (aligned with Supply and Use Tables). Used for structural analysis, multiplier studies and as a foundation for satellite accounts.
candidates.notes: Structural benchmark product. Referenced as a source in the construction of tourism and other satellite accounts. Updated with major base-year revisions of the SCNM.

proposed_edges.basis: ITAEE is produced within the Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales de México framework.
State export totals are consistent with / derived in relation to the national merchandise trade balance.
State industrial activity indicator is the geographic disaggregation of the national IMAI framework.
Informality rate is a standard published indicator derived from ENOE.
Institutional sector accounts are an integral component of the SCNM under SNA 2008.
Input-output matrix is produced as part of the national-accounts benchmark / SUT process.
Tourism satellite account draws on the Input-Output Matrix and Supply-and-Use Tables.
Programme transfers appear in household income data and are used in poverty and distribution analysis based on ENIGH.
